newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Mandela letter sent to wrong envoy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Mandela letter sent to wrong envoy.

text.p: A letter for Indonesian President Suharto from his South African counterpart Nelson Mandela concerning a jailed East Timorese rebel leader was accidentally sent to the Portuguese embassy in Pretoria, a report said on Sunday.

The absence of the letter, sent in mid-July, caused some friction between Indonesia and South Africa last week as Jakarta denied ever receiving a proposal from Mandela to free East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao.

Indonesian Foreign Ali Alatas was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying on Saturday that the receipt of the letter was delayed because it went to the embassy of East Timor's former colonial power.
Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono acknowledged receipt of the letter on Friday night after its contents had already been leaked.

"Although the letter was sent to the Indonesian embassy in Pretoria, according to a report from the mission, in fact officials of the South African presidency mistakenly sent the letter to the Portuguese embassy," Alatas said.

"This is a strange mistake and misunderstanding and all levels of the South African government, starting from the president and foreign minister to the ambassador in Jakarta, have already apologised to Indonesia," he said.
A small group of armed guerrillas are still fighting Indonesian rule in East Timor which was abandoned by colonial power Portugal in 1974.

Indonesian troops moved into East Timor with tacit Western approval in December 1975 and it was incorporated as Indonesia's 27th province the following July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.

Alatas said he had spoken to his South African counterpart Alfred Nzo about the problem and said Indonesia did not blame the official responsible for delivering the letter as he was of low rank and probably mistaken.

"What is proper for us to question is why the Portuguese embassy did not return the letter," he said, adding that the letter probably became the source of leaks in Lisbon newspapers about Mandela's request for Gusmao's release.
"I sincerely ask, where is the morality of Portugal? Keeping a letter which is not intended for them is truly disgraceful and they used that letter for disgraceful aims as well," he said.
Mandela met Gusmao, serving a 20-year sentence in a Jakarta jail for "criminal offences and illegal possession of firearms", at a secret dinner during his state visit to Indonesia in mid-July.

Mandela has since met exiled independence spokesman Jose Ramos Horta and Portuguese President Jorge Sampio in Pretoria in a peace-making role which he says will be complimentary to ongoing talks on East Timor's future under the umbrella of the office of the U.N. Secretary-General.
Suharto has accepted an invitation from Mandela to pay a state visit to South Africa but the timing was still being discussed.
